basis_words: Measured on the 15 trading days ending at the newest silver partition, using the library calendar (its hardcoded fallback answered: pandas_market_calendars absent, source NYSE/hardcoded-fallback-2010-2027). Each landing_utc is the latest LastModified of the objects under the partition (one object per partition, read from a LIST response). Earliest landing 07:46 New York; latest landing 07:46 New York; all 15 landings at or after 06:00 New York (count 15 of 15). The seconds past 11:46 UTC range from 02 to 30. For 12 of the 15 partitions the landing date is the partition date plus one calendar day. For 2026-09-23, 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25 the newest object is dated 2026-09-28 (a later write than the day after; this read did not separate a rewrite from the first write). Proposed fire time 08:15 New York: about 28 minutes after the latest landing, a margin chosen over one observed instant, not a spread (the 15 landings span 0 minutes at minute resolution). All 15 instants fall in US daylight time; the New York wall time of the same instants is one hour earlier after the November clock change, which this read did not measure. This is a proposal for the CTO's half, not a setting.

catch_up.notes: 13 catch-up dates. 2026-06-09 is the first silver partition date and gold starts at 2026-06-10, one trading day later; no silver partition exists before 2026-06-09, so no prior trading day is in silver. The producer's trading-day rule reads the prior trading day's close (data/assets/scripts/gold/irpt_holdings_performance/holdings_performance.py, _frame_for, lines 983-987); that is what the code says, and no run was made to confirm it as the cause. The other 12 dates are the trading days 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-13, after the gold newest date 2026-09-25. Five silver partitions without gold (2026-06-13, 2026-06-14, 2026-06-19, 2026-06-20, 2026-06-21) are weekend or NYSE holiday dates and are excluded by the calendar.
